# The shared-tilt positive-normal envelope fails on a monotone triangle chain

Let T be the standard two-dimensional triangle, V=|T|, and
Gamma=4/9. For positive common-vertex triangle fibers r_k T,
the positive-normal envelope is

    P_r(t)=r^2                    if t<=0;
           (r-t)^2               if 0<=t<=r/3;
           4t(r-2t)              if r/3<=t<=r/2;
           0                     if t>=r/2.                 (1)

It equals the infimum over positive continuous normals
w1,w2>=0, w1+w2=1, of the cap mass divided by V. Its complete
derivation is in `candidate 680d45e380747dc3`.
For an own-fiber centroid the relaxed shared-tilt certificate is

    E_j=inf_{beta in R} sum_k P_(r_k)(r_j/3-beta(k-j)).       (2)

For actual concave radius chains, V E_j is a valid lower bound
for the absolute depth at (j,(r_j/3,r_j/3)). It preserves one
base tilt but minimizes the continuous normal separately on each
fiber. The following example disproves sufficiency of (2), even
for a nondecreasing chain and its unique weighted-median anchor.

## 1. An exact rational example and all-anchor optimization

Take bases 0,1,2 and radii

    (r_0,r_1,r_2)=(1,3,3).                                 (3)

The differences 2,0 are nonnegative and nonincreasing. The actual
full-dimensional body is

    C={0<=z<=2, x1,x2>=0, x1+x2<=min(1+2z,3)}.

It is convex, equals the convex hull of its three lifted integer
fibers, and has exactly the prescribed fibers. Its mixed mass is
M=19V, so the proposed target is

    Gamma M/(2V)=38/9.

For every beta and every anchor, the own-fiber term in (2) is
P_(r_j)(r_j/3)=Gamma r_j^2. All other terms are nonnegative.
The following three tilts attain exactly those lower bounds:

| Anchor j | q=r_j/3 | beta | Three thresholds q-beta(k-j) | Sum of envelopes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1/3 | -3 | 1/3, 10/3, 19/3 | 4/9 |
| 1 | 1 | -1/2 | 1/2, 1, 3/2 | 4 |
| 2 | 1 | 3 | 7, 4, 1 | 4 |

Thus these are the exact infima over ALL real tilts, not merely
upper estimates from a finite grid. All original integer anchors
have been included, and

    max_j E_j=4 <38/9.                                     (4)

The strict shortfall is 2/9, and the ratio is 18/19. The middle
base 1 is the unique weighted median of the original weights
(1,9,9): its strict tails have weights 1 and 9, both below 19/2;
the other two bases fail one of these inequalities.

## 2. A complete parameter family

More generally, let

    (r_0,r_1,r_2)=(a,R,R),  R>0, 0<a<=R/3.                 (5)

This is again a positive nondecreasing concave chain. At the
middle anchor choose beta=-R/6. Its three thresholds are
R/6,R/3,R/2. The first and last envelopes vanish because
R/6>=a/2 and R/2 is the zero-area threshold for the positive
equal normal on RT. The middle envelope is Gamma R^2.

At anchor 0, beta=-2R excludes both other envelopes; at anchor 2,
beta=2R excludes both earlier ones. Together with the fixed own
term, this proves the exact all-anchor identities

    (E_0,E_1,E_2)=(Gamma a^2,Gamma R^2,Gamma R^2).

Consequently the maximum certificate falls short of its proposed
target by exactly

    (Gamma/2)(a^2+2R^2)-Gamma R^2=(Gamma/2)a^2>0.           (6)

The ratio equals 2R^2/(a^2+2R^2), with value 18/19 at a=R/3.
Every member has the same unique weighted-median base 1.

## 3. The normal relaxation is substantive, and the actual body is safe

At the middle witness tilt in (5), the last RT cap at threshold
R/2 can have zero area only for the equal normal w=(1/2,1/2).
But at the middle centroid threshold R/3 that same normal has
cap mass (5/9)R^2 V, rather than the envelope's (4/9)R^2 V.
The latter minimum requires a coordinate normal. Thus the three
individual minima in this witness cannot be realized by one
common continuous normal. This is a limitation of the relaxation,
not a contradiction to its valid lower-bound direction.

There is an exact actual all-cap safety certificate. The first
triangle aT is a subset of RT, and the other two fibers are RT.
The proved measurable-subset three-source theorem in
`candidate dafd411c026c302c`
therefore gives, at the actual middle centroid,

    A_mu(1,(R/3,R/3)) >= V[Gamma R^2+a^2/2]
                       > (Gamma/2)V[a^2+2R^2].             (7)

The surplus in (7) is (1-Gamma)a^2 V/2=5a^2 V/18.
For (1,3,3), the lower bound is 9V/2>38V/9. It controls every
oblique and vertical cap. We do not assert that (7) is the exact
actual depth.

The counterexample concerns the proposed envelope for arbitrary
fiber counts. It does not contradict the four-monotone-fiber
envelope theorem, whose two adjacent predecessors supply an
additional payment. Nor does it refute existence of an actual
sufficient own centroid or the original OC bound.

The standard-library verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_monotone_triangle_shared_tilt_envelope_counterexample.py`.
